name: Baseline
description: Endogenous fast-transition baseline: model defaults with 2025-level carbon prices and no further policy. After the 2026 accounting reconciliation (lag warm-up, automation as intermediate consumption, one efficiency series shared with demand's intensity decline), the no-policy path is growth-consistent with consensus: GDP growth ~2.3%/yr to 2050, 2050 electricity ~57k TWh (IEA STEPS ~55k), near-term electricity growth ~4%/yr (IEA 2024 actual), fossil electricity share ~11% in 2050 falling to ~0 by 2075 (vs ~35% in STEPS — the transition is still much faster than STEPS because Way-et-al learning rates keep solar+storage undercutting fossil dispatch), warming ~2.6C by 2100 (AR6-consistent marginal TCRE). GDP 2100 ~$1,000T sits between the SSP2 and SSP5 markers. Treat as the model's own no-policy trajectory, not a replication of any IEA scenario.
